skill.name: set-up-woocommerce-meta-ltv-bidding
skill.description: Use Product Metrics to set up and verify customer lifetime value bidding for a WooCommerce store in Meta Ads. Choose revenue or profit as the bidding signal.
skill.summary: Guide Meta Ads setup for observed WooCommerce customer lifetime value.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts match Markdown or routine integration steps, not shell substitution or system reconnaissance. Two alerts identify real risks: access to detailed order records and an unpinned installer. The workflow also risks exposing Meta credentials, importing order data without prior review, and selecting the wrong profit conversion.

remediation.issue: The assistant is told to request a Meta access token.
remediation.suggestion: Require token entry in the Product Metrics app. Remove instructions to solicit tokens in chat or pass them as command arguments.

remediation.issue: The initial order import can start before the merchant reviews the data transfer.
remediation.suggestion: Before importing orders or enabling delivery, have the merchant review imported fields, retention, consent settings, and approved destinations. Obtain explicit approval before each transfer.

remediation.issue: The order check can retrieve more data than needed for customer classification.
remediation.suggestion: Use a read operation that returns only customer classifications for the approved storefront. Retrieve an individual order only when necessary and explicitly authorized.

remediation.issue: The installer command does not pin the package version or skill revision.
remediation.suggestion: Document an approved installer version and a verified skill revision. Require user approval before running the installer.

remediation.issue: The profit example points to an order profit event instead of the lifetime profit event.
remediation.suggestion: Use PMProfitLTV with CUSTOMER_PROFIT_LTV for lifetime profit bidding. Have the user verify the event and purpose rule before selecting the conversion.

semantic_findings.title: Assistant Solicits a Meta Access Token
semantic_findings.description: The workflow permits the assistant to request a Meta Conversions API token and pass it to a command. This can expose it through chat, tool traces, or process arguments even when the assistant does not repeat it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide says to enter the token in the app, then says the assistant must ask for it. The skill explicitly allows passing it to a command.

semantic_findings.title: Initial Order Import Lacks a Data Review Step
semantic_findings.description: The WooCommerce guide queues an initial order import before the consent setup step. It does not first explain the imported fields, retention, or which destinations are authorized to receive data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented import precedes consent configuration, but the exact import payload and retention could not be verified. The Meta guide does describe consent checks for delivery.

semantic_findings.title: Order Profit Example Conflicts With Lifetime Profit Bidding
semantic_findings.description: The main guide points to the order profit event as a profit optimization example. Following it for lifetime profit can shift spend toward the wrong conversion signal.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The main guide names PMOrderProfit with ORDER_PROFIT, but the lifetime value guide specifies PMProfitLTV with CUSTOMER_PROFIT_LTV. The merchant must still select the conversion.

content.user_title: Set Up WooCommerce Lifetime Value Bidding in Meta
content.value_statement: A first purchase can understate what a repeat customer is worth. Use observed WooCommerce revenue or profit to configure a lifetime value conversion for Meta Ads.
actual_capabilities: Checks Product Metrics setup status through the CLI or MCP and identifies unfinished steps.
Guides WooCommerce plugin setup and the connection to a Meta pixel or dataset.
Checks whether recent paid orders are classified as new or returning.
Explains how consent and cost coverage affect revenue and profit lifetime value events.
Guides test event verification and custom conversion setup in Meta Events Manager.
Explains how to choose a lifetime value conversion and review a return on ad spend goal.
limitations: The setup requires Product Metrics Pro, WordPress administrator access, and access to the Meta pixel or dataset.
You create the custom conversion and select it in Meta. The assistant does not change campaign optimization.
Lifetime value reflects observed paid orders for one connected store. It does not predict future value or combine history across stores.
Lifetime value events require a recognized customer and eligible consent. Profit events also require complete order costs.

use_cases.title: Check Setup Readiness
use_cases.description: Find which WooCommerce and Meta connections are ready and which setup steps still need attention.

use_cases.title: Test a Revenue Conversion
use_cases.description: Verify delivery of a revenue lifetime value event before selecting the custom conversion in one Meta ad set.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Missing Profit Events
use_cases.description: Check whether product, payment, or shipping costs are missing before proposing a profit lifetime value conversion.

prompt_templates.title: List Setup Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: What do I need to connect my WooCommerce store to Meta for revenue lifetime value bidding?
prompt_templates.scenario: You are planning your first setup.

prompt_templates.title: Check Connection Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the setup status for my selected WooCommerce property. Tell me what is ready and what I need to do. Do not change any settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: The plugin is installed, but you are not sure whether event delivery is active.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Revenue Event
prompt_templates.prompt: Walk me through a consented test order and show me how to verify the revenue lifetime value event in Meta. Do not change my campaign.
prompt_templates.scenario: The store and Meta dataset are connected.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Profit LTV Pilot
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me check consent and cost coverage for Profit LTV. Confirm which Meta event and purpose rule I should use. Suggest a pilot for one ad set without changing any settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Revenue tracking works, and you are evaluating profit bidding.

output_examples.input: Why does the profit lifetime value event not appear after my test order?
output: Check that the test customer granted analytics and ad user data consent.
Confirm that each required cost is recorded for the test order.
Once Meta receives PMProfitLTV, use CUSTOMER_PROFIT_LTV as the purpose rule.

output_examples.input: My revenue lifetime value test arrived in Meta. What comes next?
output: Clear the test event code so future events are not limited to Test events.
Create a custom conversion for PMRevenueLTV with the CUSTOMER_REVENUE_LTV purpose rule.
Select the custom conversion in one ad set and review its delivery before expanding.

best_practices: Enter the Meta token in the Product Metrics app and keep it out of chat.
Confirm the store, dataset, and consent settings before importing orders or sending events.
Verify the lifetime value event and purpose rule before testing a new bidding goal in one ad set.
anti_patterns: Do not use the order profit conversion as a substitute for lifetime profit.
Do not copy the return goal from an ordinary purchase conversion without reviewing the new signal.
Do not leave the test event code enabled when you expect live reporting.

faq.question: Do I need Product Metrics Pro?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented WooCommerce setup uses Pro and the Product Metrics WordPress plugin.

faq.question: How does it identify repeat customers?
faq.answer: It uses the WooCommerce account, then the billing email for guest orders, then the phone number.

faq.question: Does the event value include the customer's entire history?
faq.answer: The event value is what the current order adds. The observed running total is a separate field when available.

faq.question: When is a Profit LTV event sent?
faq.answer: The customer must be recognized and grant the required consent. The order must have complete costs. A loss is sent as zero.

faq.question: Why can I not find my lifetime value event in Meta?
faq.answer: Meta must first receive the event. Place an eligible test order and confirm delivery in Events Manager.

faq.question: Will the assistant switch my campaign to lifetime value bidding?
faq.answer: No. The assistant guides you, but you create and select the custom conversion in Meta.
